headline: Death penalty possible as Cabinet approves draft law criminalizing enforced disappearance
summary: The new legislation aims to tackle forced disappearances, with the maximum penalty for the offense being the death penalty.
details: The Bangladesh Cabinet has officially approved a draft law that makes enforced disappearances a criminal offense. This move comes as a significant step toward addressing human rights concerns and legal gaps in the country.

Under the proposed law, the maximum penalty for those found guilty of enforced disappearance will be the death penalty. This strict measure is intended to serve as adent deterrent against such practices.
The draft law was approved during a cabinet meeting presided over by the Chief Advisor. The legislation will now move forward for final legal processing and final approval.
The move is seen as a critical development in ensuring accountability and providing justice for the victims and their families who have suffered from forced disappearances.
caption:
Death penalty for enforced disappearances. The Bangladesh Cabinet has approved a draft law to criminalize the act.

The Bangladesh Cabinet has officially approved a draft law that makes enforced disappearances a criminal offense. This move comes as a significant step toward addressing human rights concerns and legal gaps in the country.

Under the proposed law, the maximum penalty for those found guilty of enforced disappearance will be the death penalty. This strict measure is intended to serve as adent deterrent against such practices.

The draft law was approved during a cabinet meeting presided over by the Chief Advisor. The legislation will now move forward for final legal processing and final approval.

The move is seen as a critical development in ensuring accountability and providing justice for the victims and their families who have suffered from forced disappearances.

headline: Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister arrives in Dhaka on official visit
summary: Engineer Waleed Al-Khereiji is in Bangladesh for a two-day visit to discuss trade, investment, and regional security.
details: Saudi Arabian Deputy Foreign Minister Engineer Waleed Al-Khereiji has arrived in Bangladesh for a brief two-day official visit.
He was received at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Monday night by Humayun Kabir, the Foreign Affairs Adviser to the Chief Adviser.
During his stay, the Deputy Minister is scheduled to hold several high-level bilateral meetings with top government officials and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Key topics for discussion are expected to include trade, investment, the labor market, and regional security issues.
The Saudi official is scheduled to depart Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon following the conclusion of his short visit.
caption:
Saudi Deputy Foreign Minister Waleed Al-Khereiji has arrived in Dhaka for high-level talks on trade and security.

Saudi Arabian Deputy Foreign Minister Engineer Waleed Al-Khereiji has arrived in Bangladesh for a brief two-day official visit.

He was received at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Monday night by Humayun Kabir, the Foreign Affairs Adviser to the Chief Adviser.

During his stay, the Deputy Minister is scheduled to hold several high-level bilateral meetings with top government officials and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Key topics for discussion are expected to include trade, investment, the labor market, and regional security issues.

The Saudi official is scheduled to depart Dhaka on Tuesday afternoon following the conclusion of his short visit.
